sources.author: Swyx (Shawn Wang)
sources.headline: AI Engineer @ Latent Space | Building the AI Engineer community
sources.post_summary: We just crossed 100k AI Engineers in our community. 18 months ago this title didn't exist. What changed: the stack stabilized. Embeddings → RAG → agents → evals. Every company now has at least one person whose full-time job is prompt routing and context window budgeting. The job title won.

sources.author: Lilian Weng
sources.headline: Head of Safety Research @ OpenAI
sources.post_summary: The hardest unsolved problem in agentic AI isn't reasoning — it's interruption. When should an agent stop and ask? Too often: useless. Too rarely: catastrophic. We've been studying this in production systems and the failure modes are consistent: agents over-index on task completion and under-index on state uncertainty. Sharing a framework we use internally to think about confidence thresholds for autonomous action.

sources.author: Greg Brockman
sources.headline: President @ OpenAI
sources.post_summary: Something subtle happened in the last 6 months: AI infrastructure spend became a competitive moat, not just a cost center. The companies buying inference capacity at scale now aren't doing it for a chatbot. They're pre-positioning for workflows that don't exist yet. This is the same logic behind AWS in 2008. The infra bet is the product bet.

sources.author: Alex Goodman
sources.headline: Founder @ BuildShip | No-code AI workflow automation
sources.post_summary: We analyzed 10,000 AI automations built on our platform last quarter. The #1 use case isn't content or customer support anymore — it's internal data routing. Someone asks a question in Slack, an agent pulls from 4 different internal tools, synthesizes an answer, and logs the interaction. Boring? Yes. High ROI? Completely. The enterprise AI wave isn't flashy. It's plumbing.

sources.author: Kyle Coleman
sources.headline: CMO at Clari | GTM Strategy | Pipeline Generation | AI in Sales
sources.post_summary: Most teams are using AI to do more outbound. The winners are using AI to do better outbound. I ran a 90-day test: AI-personalized sequences at 20% of the volume outperformed spray-and-pray by 3x on booked meetings. The era of signal-based selling is here and most stacks aren't built for it yet.

sources.author: Jess Schultz
sources.headline: Founder @ Amplify GTM | RevOps Advisor | HubSpot & Salesforce Architect
sources.post_summary: RevOps is becoming the most political job in a company. You own the data everyone argues about, the tools everyone blames, and the attribution nobody agrees on. The best RevOps leaders I've seen stop trying to be neutral and start acting like product managers — owning decisions, not just systems.

sources.author: Devin Reed
sources.headline: Head of Content Strategy @ Clari | Ex-Gong | I write about content that drives pipeline
sources.post_summary: Your content calendar is a vanity project if it's not connected to pipeline stages. We mapped every content asset to a buyer journey phase and killed 40% of what we were producing. Engagement went down. Pipeline influenced went up 28%. Fewer pieces, more intent — that's the shift most B2B content teams need to make.

sources.author: Tamara Schwartz
sources.headline: GTM Engineer @ Series B SaaS | Clay + Apollo + AI Workflows | Outbound Infrastructure
sources.post_summary: Spent 3 months building a GTM stack that replaces 4 SDRs with 1 engineer and a $900/month tool budget. Clay for enrichment and signals, Apollo for sequencing, Claude for personalization at scale, Attio as the source of truth. Not saying you should fire your SDRs — saying you should 10x what one can do. Here's the full build.

sources.author: Priya Nair
sources.headline: Founder @ Stackform | Building AI-native B2B tools | prev. Stripe
sources.post_summary: Shipped our first paid feature with zero marketing spend — just a Loom demo posted in three Slack communities. 47 signups in 48 hours. The lesson: distribution is a product decision, not an afterthought. Here's exactly what we sent and where.

sources.author: Marcus Webb
sources.headline: Solo dev turned SaaS founder | $0 → $8k MRR in 6 months | Claude Code daily driver
sources.post_summary: I quit my $180k eng job 7 months ago to build solo. People said I was crazy. Last week I crossed $8k MRR. I'm not posting this to flex — I'm posting it because the biggest thing that held me back was not believing it was possible without a co-founder or VC. Here's what actually moved the needle.

sources.author: Jordan Kim
sources.headline: Product Engineer | Career pivoter (teacher → dev, 2023) | Building @Clarifai side project
sources.post_summary: 18 months ago I was grading essays. This week I shipped a feature used by 2,000 people. No bootcamp magic — just obsessive consistency: 1 hour of code every morning before school, then 2 hours after. The pivot wasn't about talent. It was about not letting the gap between where I was and where I wanted to be feel permanent.

sources.author: Leila Santos
sources.headline: Co-founder @ Draftly | AI writing tools for GTM teams | formerly HubSpot PM
sources.post_summary: We almost killed our startup last month. User growth was flat, burn was accelerating, and my co-founder and I hadn't agreed on the core ICP in weeks. What saved us: a 4-hour whiteboard session where we finally said out loud what we both knew but were avoiding. Brutal honesty is a product strategy. Here's what we cut and why it immediately unblocked us.
